correctness.rationale: The universal two-level reduction applies to the symmetric homogeneous quartic H_lambda by Riener Theorem 1.3 (independently Blekherman--Riener Proposition 3.1). The rational branch formula is an exact evaluation; its derivative numerator has the stated factorization, checked algebraically and in the actual package. For eight atoms, each multiplicity branch is bounded using explicit positive polynomial gaps and the winning branch has a uniquely determined global maximum at the sole negative zero of q(t). The probability moment proof establishes the universal bound and forces irrational mass at equality; compactness then gives strict finite n and a two-level rational approximation gives the limiting norm. The package checker replayed successfully; finite experiments are not substituted for infinite arguments.

value.rationale: Mean reflection is a canonical rank-one involution and, after dyadic sign conjugation, a one-Haar-coefficient sign change: its sharp L4 norm quantifies stability of a specific finite averaging symmetry. The full finite-n algebraic profile, first nontrivial n=8 exact optimal polynomial, and strict all-n rational-atom gap to a sharp irrational extremizer provide a mathematically motivated finite-versus-nonatomic phenomenon. This is a natural exact invariant with a structural explanation, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice or a generic finite brute-force table.
